1 1 . This is an appeal filed under Section 29 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act,
2005 (hereinafter referred to as D.V. Act) r/w Section 413 BNSS against the order dated 05.08.2024 passed by Ld. JMFC (Central) (Mahila Court)-03 in CC No. 6692/2020 titled as Radha Vs. Sandeep Kumar whereby Ld. Trial Court had directed to respondent no. 1 to pay maintenance @ Rs.4500/-
to appellant no. 1 and Rs. 4000/- per month to the child with annual increment @ 10% every year.
2.

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case as necessary for the disposal of the present appeal are that the marriage between appellant no. 1 and respondent no. 1 was solemnized on 12.12.2002.
Out of the wedlock one child i.e. appellant no. 2 was born.
It is the case of appellant that she was treated with cruelty by the respondents.

She was mentally harassed and was thrown out of the house on 20.12.2003 however,
with the intervention of the respectable members of society she was again taken back.

It is the case of appellant that on 07.12.2004, respondents in a planned manner pour kerosene oil and the appellants somehow managed to save themselves and since then appellants are residing separately.

The appellants lodged an FIR bearing no. 81/2005 u/s 406/498A/307/506/34 IPC, after facing trial the respondents were convicted, appeal against the said order is pending before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court.
3. Since, respondent no. 1 failed to maintain the appellants CA No.: 372/2024 Radha Vs. Sandeep Kumar & Ors.

It is stated that respondent no.1 is not clearing the arrears and the respondents are not allowing the petitioners to enter the house.
It is stated that respondent no. 1 is a well qualified person and earning more than Rs.1 Lakh per month and thus, a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month should be granted.
The appellants preferred a complaint u/s 12 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act (herein after referred to as DV Act).

Respondent no. 1 chose not to appear and he was proceeded ex-parte.
Respondent no. 2 and 3 who are the in-laws, who appeared and filed their reply.
Vide order dated 02.08.2023, the Ld. MM adjourned the interim application till the disposal of the main petition.
The appellants herein filed an appeal and the said order was set aside by Ld. Special Judge, NDPS vide order dated 25.01.2024.
Thereafter, after hearing arguments the Ld. MM passed the impugned order.
Hence, the present appeal.

sentences.text: It is submitted that no rent towards alternative accommodation was granted thus, the order is liable to be set aside.

It is submitted that Ld. Trial Court has failed to take into consideration that respondent/husband was working with Bajaj Finance and without any basis awarded maintenance by assessing the income as per Minimum Wages Act.
6.
No arguments have been addressed on behalf of the respondents despite opportunity.
7. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the appellant and perused the record.
8. It is the grievance of the appellant that enhanced maintenance has not been granted despite the fact that the respondent no. 1 is earning more than Rs.1 Lakh per month.

9. It is undisputed that appellants were granted a sum of Rs.
12,000/- as maintenance by the Ld. Principal Judge, Family Court and the said order has neither been set aside or varied.
10. It has been held by Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Kamal Singh v. Kanta Bangari, 2023 SCC Online Del 7925 that CA No.: 372/2024 Radha Vs. Sandeep Kumar & Ors.

any prayer for enhancement has to be made before the Court which had granted the maintenance amount after placing reliance upon the judgment of Rajneesh v. Neha, (2021), 2 SCC 324.

The relevant para is reproduced as under :
"37.

Such conflicting Orders, in the similar facts and without any change in circumstances, under overlapping jurisdiction of different Acts, creates a sense of judicial impropriety and forum shopping, which may not be conducive to the majesty of the Courts.

To avoid conflicting orders and overcome this issue of overlapping jurisdiction, the Apex Court in Rajnesh (supra) laid down certain guidelines which are reproduced herein below : -
"128.1.

(i) Where successive claims for maintenance are made by a party under different statutes, the court would consider an adjustment or set-off, of the amount awarded in the previous proceeding(s), while determining whether any further amount is to be awarded in the subsequent proceeding.
128.2. (ii) It is made mandatory for the applicant to disclose the previous proceeding and the orders passed therein, in the subsequent proceeding.
128.3. (iii) If the order passed in the previous proceeding(s) requires any modification or variation, it would be required to be done in the same proceeding."

38. The Apex Court has, therefore, clarified in aforementioned Judgment that each of the statutes has their own independent jurisdiction and scope to adjudicate the maintenance application, the invocation/grant of remedy under one statute does not oust the jurisdiction to entertain the claim Radha And Anr vs Sandeep Kumar And Ors on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64011566/
3 for maintenance under the other Acts.

11. Ld. counsel for the appellant has vehemently argued and placed reliance on the statement of account of respondent no. 1 to argue that he is receiving a sum of Rs. 52,000/- as salary from Bajaj Finance.
12. The statement of account on which reliance is placed was duly considered by the Ld. Family Court which had awarded a sum of Rs. 12,000/- as reflected from the order dated 29.09.2016.
The Ld. JMFC was neither sitting in appeal nor in revision over the order of the Ld. Family Court.

There is no fresh document on record which could suggest that he is still employed with Bajaj Finance or that he is earning more than Rs. 1 Lakh.
13.
The appellants in essence were seeking enhancement of the amount of maintenance granted by the Ld. Family Court.

The appellants ought to have filed an application u/s 127 Cr.P.C. seeking enhancement of the amount of maintenance although there was no bar to filing of the application under Section 12 of the D.V. Act before the Ld. JMFC but no additional material was placed by the appellants before the Ld. JMFC.
Be that as it may be.
14. The Ld. Trial Court was left with no option but to assess the income on the basis of Minimum Wages Act.
I do not find any infirmity in the said approach and the Ld. Trial Court rightly placed reliance upon the notification under CA No.: 372/2024 Radha Vs. Sandeep Kumar & Ors.

Hence, no error can be found within the findings of the Ld. Trial Court wherein the income has been assessed to be Rs. 21,215/-.
15.
In so far as prayer for alternate accommodation was concerned, the Ld. JMFC noted that alternate relief of amount of rent has already been granted.
The Ld. JMFC has granted consolidated amount which also include the amount of rent primarily on the ground that appellants are residing separately.
In the detailed affidavit of assets and liabilities the appellant no. 1 has claimed that she is residing with her parents.
16. It is undisputed fact that appellants are residing separately since 07.12.2004 and the present petition came to be filed in the year 2020.
A prayer was made in the interim application seeking right of residence or same level of alternate accommodation.
The Ld. Trial Court had granted consolidated amount which includes rent as maintenance in regard to the prayer of alternative accommodation.

In so far as right of residence in the same house was concerned it is the own case of appellants that they were thrown out of the matrimonial house on 07.12.2004 so after passage of Radha And Anr vs Sandeep Kumar And Ors on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64011566/
4 sixteen years the same was rightly refused.
17.
